title: String Theory export
description: One JSON file per surface. An app export carries the application's own UI strings with a pixel budget, so a human can rewrite them and the app can merge the rewrites back by id. A docs export carries the prose a project ships to its readers — README, changelog, release notes, guides — with no font and no budgets. Canonical form only: the loader also accepts documented aliases, but an exporter should emit exactly these names.

format.description: Format id. Optional on input, always written on output.

app.description: Application name. Shown in the header, used for the export filename.

context.description: One line about the screen or feature, sent with every AI prompt.

surface.description: What kind of file this is. `app` holds the application's own UI strings and carries a layout. `docs` holds the prose a project ships: README, changelog, release notes, guides. A docs file has no font and no pixel or character budgets.

source.description: For a docs file: the document path inside the repository, such as "README.md" or "docs/guide.md".

order.description: For a docs file: lane order inside the project. README 0, changelog 1, release notes 2, then the documents the README links to, in link order.

title.description: For a docs file: the name shown on the file pill, such as "README.md".

defaultMaxPx.description: Older name for defaultMaxPxPerLine. Accepted on input, never written.

defaultMaxPxPerLine.description: Line budget for strings that do not carry their own maxPxPerLine.

font.description: The font the pixel figures are measured in. Must match what the app renders with.

family.description: Font family name, for example 'Segoe UI'. Fallback stacks are allowed.

weight.description: Numeric weight preferred. Strings are wider at heavier weights.

letterSpacing.description: Extra tracking in CSS pixels, added per character.

id.description: Stable id from the app catalogue. Unique per file.

text.description: The string as it ships today. Keep it on one line; a newline is measured at the widest line.

where.description: The line of UI where the string appears. Shown on hover and sent to the model.

maxPxPerLine.description: Width of one line: the box the text wraps inside, measured in the file font.

maxLines.description: How many lines the layout allows this string.

maxPxTotal.description: Total budget, normally maxPxPerLine x maxLines. Recomputed when it disagrees.

font.description: Measurement override for a string that does not use the file font.

maxChars.description: Character ceiling, only when the app enforces one itself.

state.description: Written by the tool on export: untouched, in progress, or reviewed. Importers may ignore it.

px.description: Optional: the app's own measurement. Only used for the budget when maxPx is absent.

tags.description: What the string does. The first tag is its role from the shared vocabulary; further tags group strings that belong together, and a project may add its own.

note.description: A free sentence of context the layout cannot express. Never a rewrite.
